text: {"answerable": false, "answer": "The passages do not show DiffTRe being used to fit a diffusion coefficient. In the DiffTRe paper, the targets were oxygen RDF, ADF and pressure, and the self-diffusion coefficient D was only a held-out observable [W3168247670#017]. The learned model overestimated D (10.91 vs. 2.2 μm2/ms experimental) [W3168247670#017]. DiffTRe differentiates only through the potential energy computation of decorrelated states, not through the whole trajectory [W3168247670#012]. The passages do not say whether this suffices for a dynamical property like D. A different differentiable-simulation method did fit diffusion coefficients, using gradients of the Green-Kubo diffusion coefficient for Lennard-Jones particles and combined density and IR fitting for water [W4406553977#010][W4406553977#018]. That work does not describe DiffTRe, so it does not answer your question."}
